You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
Yes — Airplane Mode is very likely the reason you're still not getting service. It turns off all of your phone's wireless radios, including the cellular connection, so your line can be active on our end but still show "No Service" on the device.

Please turn it off:
1. Swipe down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings panel.
2. Find the **Airplane Mode** icon (it looks like a small airplane) — tap it so it's no longer highlighted/enabled.

Once it's off, wait about 30 seconds and check the top of your screen again for signal bars and a network indicator (like 5G or LTE). Let me know what you see.

I understand the frustration — let's work through the remaining device-side causes. Two things are showing at once: **No Signal** and **Data Disabled**. Let's clear the simplest one first.

**Please turn mobile data back on:**
1. Open **Settings** → **Network & internet** (or "Connections" on some phones).
2. Tap **Mobile network** / **SIMs**.
3. Toggle **Mobile data** to **ON**.

If your quick settings panel is easier, swipe down from the top of the screen and tap the **Mobile data** tile so it's enabled.

Once that's on, wait about 30 seconds and tell me what the status bar shows now — specifically whether you have signal bars and whether a network type (5G, LTE, 4G) appears. That will tell me whether we're dealing with just a data setting or a deeper connection problem.
Let me rule out anything on the account side before we go further into device troubleshooting.

Thanks for trying that. Since your line is active on our end and your data usage is well within your 15 GB limit (8.7 GB used), this is pointing to something on the device or SIM itself.

**Next step — please reseat your SIM card:**
1. Power your phone **off** completely.
2. Locate the SIM tray (usually on the side of the phone) and eject it using the SIM eject tool or a small paperclip.
3. Remove the SIM, check it's clean and undamaged, then reinsert it firmly and close the tray.
4. Power the phone back **on**.

Wait about 30–60 seconds after it boots, then check the status bar again for signal bars.

Please let me know what you see after that. If there's still no signal, I'll have you check the SIM status specifically to see whether the card is being recognized at all or whether it's locked — and if it turns out to be locked or not recognized, I'll need to escalate you to our technical support team for hands-on SIM assistance.

Good — that rules out a faulty or missing SIM, so we've eliminated the most common hardware cause. Let's look at the software settings next.

**Please check your APN settings:**
1. Open **Settings** → **Network & internet** (or "Connections").
2. Tap **Mobile network** → **Access Point Names** (APN).
3. Look at what's listed — specifically whether the settings appear blank, unexpected, or flagged as incorrect.

If anything looks off, tap the **three-dot menu** (top right) → **Reset to default**, then **restart your phone** for the change to take effect.

Please let me know what you see, or whether the reset helped. If the APN settings look correct and you're still showing "No Signal," the next thing I'll have you check is your preferred network mode — if the phone is set to an older technology like 2G, it can fail to latch onto the network even when everything else is fine.

Yes, please go ahead and reset it.

1. Open **Settings** → **Network & internet** (or "Connections") → **Mobile network**.
2. Tap **Access Point Names** (APN).
3. Tap the **three-dot menu** (usually top right corner) → **Reset to default**.
4. Once it's reset, **restart your phone**.

The reboot is important — the new APN settings won't apply until the device restarts.

After it powers back on, wait about 30–60 seconds and check the status bar for signal bars and a network type (5G, LTE, 4G). Let me know what you see — if the signal is back, we're done. If it's still showing "No Signal," we'll check your preferred network mode next.

You're very welcome — glad we got it sorted!

To recap what we did for your line ending in **2002**:
- Cleared the **overdue bill** (B1234321, $65.00 — now paid)
- **Reactivated** the suspended line
- Turned off **Airplane Mode** and re-enabled **mobile data**
- Reset the **APN settings** to default — this turned out to be the actual cause

Your line is now showing as **Active** on our end with 5G and mobile data working.

One heads-up: your data usage is **8.7 GB of your 15 GB** allowance for this cycle, which ends **2025-02-28**, so you've got some room left. You also have a separate issued bill (B1002, $150.00) due **2025-02-19** covering all three lines — let me know if you'd like to take care of that now or review your plan options.

Anything else I can help with?
turns.execution_output: User: No, that's everything for now — I'll leave the other bill for later. Thanks again for getting my service back up and running!
